_comment: irace-evo configuration: what the LLM may change, how to build it, which model to ask, and how to test a variant. Paths are relative to irace's execDir. Every option here is read by irace-evo; see examples/tsp-ga-evolution/code-evolution.json for a filled-in file.

problem_context.comment: J in the paper: the problem and the algorithm, in words. It goes into every prompt; the clearer it is, the better the variants.
problem_context.problem_description: What an instance is and what a solution is
problem_context.algorithm_approach: The algorithm being tuned, in one sentence
key_challenges: What makes the function hard to get right
problem_context.performance_considerations: How often the function is called, what it must not cost
problem_context.domain_knowledge: Heuristics or facts about the problem the LLM can use

source_config.comment: The one function of source_file the LLM may rewrite. Variants keep its signature. The executable of the original must be bin/<source_file without extension>, which is what the target runner runs for configurations not paired with a variant.

build_config.comment: Only the section of the chosen language is used. A variant is compiled from a temporary copy of source_file; the directory of source_file is always on the C++ include path.

llm_config.comment: api_provider: anthropic or openai. Leave api_key empty and export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY. temperature and top_p are Phi in the paper (its experiments used 1.0 and 0.9); top_p is sent only when present, and a model that refuses them is called without them, with a warning. max_retries is per variant. Optional: prompt_template (path to a file replacing the built-in prompt), temperature_range {enabled, min, max} (a random temperature per iteration), use_dynamic_prompting and elite_preservation (both off by default; neither is part of the method in the paper).

evolution_config.comment: evolution_focus_iteration is ef in the paper: before that iteration the prompts ask for moderate changes that keep the function's logic, from it on for broader structural changes. available_strategies are taken in turn, one per variant; built in: improve_efficiency, add_randomization, modify_logic, innovate_heuristic_design, conservative_improvement, hybrid_approach, problem_specific. A variant that does not compile is sent back to the LLM with the compiler error up to max_error_correction_attempts times. custom_strategies: [{name, description, ...}] adds your own.

validation_config.comment: Each variant that compiles runs once as: <variant> test_arguments, in execDir. It races only if it exits with status 0 within test_timeout seconds and a line of its output matches expected_output_pattern. Without test_arguments, compiling is the only check.
